hypothesis: For identical synthetic source screenshots, a non-occluding border ruler improves paired normalized target-center localization error over RAW without reducing target-hit correctness or increasing false selection on absent-target controls.
treatment: RAW versus BORDER_RULER only. Ruler ticks/labels occupy pre-reserved blank 72px left and 64px top margins; source UI pixels, dimensions, coordinates, and prompts are otherwise identical.

allocation.per_case_order: deterministically counterbalanced from case index; fixed before calls

decision.retain_scoped: RULER positive-case hit count is not lower than RAW; absent-target false-selection count is not higher; and paired mean normalized center error improves by at least 0.02 screen-diagonals. All source maps and response payloads audit with zero errors.
decision.reject_scoped: Any correctness regression or no material paired error improvement with complete valid evidence.
decision.hold: Fewer than 8 valid positive paired responses, model/transport/provenance mismatch, or independent audit cannot bind every response to source and arm.

controls: Same exact source PNG bytes for paired arms.
Same task prompt and source-normalized JSON schema for both arms.
No clicks, OS input, provider cloud calls, user data, GUI mutation, or model updates.
First outcome retained; a call failure is not silently retried.
Ruler pixels are restricted to pre-reserved blank margins; target/UI pixels are unchanged.
limits: Synthetic rendered controls only; no real-application or unseen-real-layout claim.
One local quantized model, one PC, 12 paired cases; exploratory screening only.
This tests visual presentation, not training/fine-tuning or action authority.
No token-cost inference from PNG bytes or local model output length.
